requirements.title: BIND(C) derived types interoperate with matching C structure types by component order
requirements.source: S18.3.4, J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF526 and PDF527.
requirements.definition: Interoperability between a Fortran derived type and a C structure type is provided by the BIND attribute; a derived type is interoperable with a C structure type exactly with BIND(C), the same number of components, interoperable corresponding component variables, and correspondence by the same relative component position.

pending.bind-attribute-provides-struct-interoper: Guard C_INT > 0 and C_DOUBLE > 0 before declaring these kinds. Mixed plan defines TYPE, BIND(C) :: pair with INTEGER(C_INT) code and REAL(C_DOUBLE) weight initialized to sentinels -777 and -9.0; C fills struct fields with 42 and exactly 1.5, and Fortran verifies both changed values. Reverse direction in the same companion has Fortran fill code=24 and weight=2.5; C reads those fields and returns exact checksum 245, proving Fortran-to-C structure transfer as well as C-to-Fortran transfer.
pending.same-component-count-required: Positive mixed plan uses exactly two Fortran components and exactly two C struct members; source-control companion records a one-member Fortran variant as non-interoperable without expecting a diagnostic from this unnumbered definition.
pending.component-variable-interoperability-requ: Guard C_INT > 0, C_DOUBLE > 0, and C_CHAR > 0 before declaring these kinds. Mixed plan uses scalar, nested, and array components: TYPE, BIND(C) :: inner has INTEGER(C_INT) :: ci and REAL(C_DOUBLE) :: cd; TYPE, BIND(C) :: outer has TYPE(inner) :: nested, INTEGER(C_INT) :: v(3), and CHARACTER(KIND=C_CHAR,LEN=1) :: tag. Matching C structs use struct inner { int ci; double cd; } and struct outer { struct inner nested; int v[3]; char tag; }. C fills nested.ci=7, nested.cd=2.25, v={4,5,6}, tag=M; Fortran verifies nested%ci=7, nested%cd=2.25, v=[4,5,6], and tag=M from nonmatching sentinels. Reverse direction has Fortran fill nested%ci=8, nested%cd=3.5, v=[10,20,30], tag=R; C checks those exact members and returns exact checksum 104.
pending.relative-position-determines-corresponde: Guard C_INT > 0 and C_DOUBLE > 0 before declaring these kinds. Mixed plan gives different component names on the C and Fortran sides but the same relative order: C writes first integer 11 and second double 2.5, Fortran components named right and left receive exact 11 and 2.5, proving names are not the correspondence oracle. A companion with Fortran names left/right filled as 13 and 4.5 is read by C fields first/second and returns exact checksum 175, proving the Fortran-to-C direction uses the same positional correspondence.

requirements.title: BIND(C) derived types cannot also have the SEQUENCE attribute
requirements.definition: A derived type with the BIND attribute shall not have the SEQUENCE attribute.

pending.bind-derived-type-no-sequence-attribute: Rejected program: MODULE m uses ISO_C_BINDING and defines TYPE, BIND(C) :: record; SEQUENCE; INTEGER(C_INT) :: value; END TYPE. Positive control deletes only the SEQUENCE statement, retains BIND(C), record, value, and INTEGER(C_INT), and then declares TYPE(record) :: x.

requirements.title: BIND(C) derived types cannot have type parameters
requirements.definition: A derived type with the BIND attribute shall not have type parameters.

pending.bind-derived-type-no-type-parameters: Rejected program: MODULE m uses ISO_C_BINDING and defines TYPE, BIND(C) :: record(k); INTEGER, KIND :: k; INTEGER(C_INT) :: value; END TYPE. Positive control changes exactly the constrained property by using TYPE, BIND(C) :: record with the same INTEGER(C_INT) :: value component and no type-parameter declaration; it is checked against the other 18.3.4 rules: it has no SEQUENCE, no EXTENDS, no type-bound-procedure part, at least one component, and an interoperable nonpointer nonallocatable data component.

requirements.title: BIND(C) derived type definitions cannot have a type-bound-procedure part
requirements.definition: A derived-type-def that defines a derived type with the BIND attribute shall not have a type-bound-procedure-part.

pending.bind-derived-type-no-type-bound-procedur: Rejected program: MODULE m uses ISO_C_BINDING and defines TYPE, BIND(C) :: record; INTEGER(C_INT) :: value; CONTAINS; PROCEDURE, NOPASS :: touch; END TYPE, plus contained SUBROUTINE touch. Positive control removes only the type-bound-procedure part and keeps the same type, component, and module subroutine; the control has declarations before module procedures and satisfies C1801, C1802, C1803, C1805, and C1806.

requirements.title: Every BIND(C) derived-type component is nonpointer, nonallocatable, data, and interoperable
requirements.definition: Each component of a derived type with the BIND attribute shall be a nonpointer, nonallocatable data component with interoperable type and type parameters.

pending.bind-component-nonpointer: Rejected program changes the sole INTEGER(C_INT) :: value component of a BIND(C) type to INTEGER(C_INT), POINTER :: value; positive control removes only POINTER and keeps the component name, type, and type parameter. The control has BIND(C), one component, no type parameters, no SEQUENCE, no EXTENDS, and no type-bound-procedure part.
pending.bind-component-nonallocatable: Rejected program changes the sole INTEGER(C_INT) :: value component of a BIND(C) type to INTEGER(C_INT), ALLOCATABLE :: value; positive control removes only ALLOCATABLE and keeps the component name, type, and type parameter. The control satisfies every other 18.3.4 constraint.
pending.bind-component-data-component: Positive control uses a data component INTEGER(C_INT) :: value. No isolated diagnostic source is portable for a non-data procedure component because procedure components are pointer components too, overlapping the nonpointer half of the same numbered constraint.
pending.bind-component-interoperable-type-parame: Rejected program changes the sole CHARACTER(KIND=C_CHAR,LEN=1) :: value component to LEN=2; positive control changes only LEN back to 1 and keeps BIND(C), the component name, type, and kind. The control satisfies every other 18.3.4 constraint.

requirements.title: No Fortran type interoperates with C bit-field, flexible-array, or union types
requirements.definition: There is no Fortran type interoperable with a C structure type containing a bit field or flexible array member, and no Fortran type interoperable with a C union type.

pending.no-fortran-type-for-c-bit-field-structur: No portable finite oracle can prove absence of every Fortran counterpart for a C bit-field structure; future source-use checks must avoid claiming interoperation with such a C struct.
pending.no-fortran-type-for-c-flexible-array-str: No portable finite oracle can prove absence of every Fortran counterpart for a flexible-array-member C struct; future mixed tests use only fixed-size C struct members.
pending.no-fortran-type-for-c-union: No portable finite oracle can prove absence of every Fortran counterpart for a C union; future mixed tests do not treat any BIND(C) derived type as interoperable with a C union.

accounting.rationale: Introduces BIND(C) as the source of Fortran/C structure interoperability.
Restates syntax/constraint consequences and C_PTR/C_FUNPTR examples; it is a NOTE.
Mixed BIND(C), component count, component interoperability, and positional correspondence definition split into fine units.
Defines BIND(C) as an eligibility condition for derived-type/C-structure interoperability.
Defines corresponding components by relative position.
States names of corresponding components need not match; it is a NOTE.
Example only; no normative requirement is based on it.
Explains why C compatible-type name rules were not adopted; it is a NOTE.

review_rationale: Source registration for 18.3 and 18.3.1-18.3.6: interoperability of intrinsic types, C pointer types, derived types and C structures, and scalar and array variables (batch242). Every unit hash-verified by an independent reviewer across two rounds; C1801-C1806 had no existing tests, and every correspondence is planned as a mixed Fortran/C program with hand-derived values. 18.3.7 (already on main) is untouched. Source accounting only.
